summary.one_liner: A chaptered tutorial that teaches how Express.js works internally by rebuilding a minimal version of the library from scratch.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a series of chapters that walk through building the express library step by step, with running examples at each stage. The author says they reuse Express's own code, variable names, and structure so readers can later contribute to the real project. The table of contents lists chapters on building the core abstractions, routing out of the box, implementing the next function, extending the response object, and adding send and json methods to the response. A chapter on error handling is marked as work in progress. The README says a minimal working library and its tutorial are complete, while the rest is still in progress.
use_cases: learn how Express middleware and next() work
step-by-step tutorial on building a web framework
study Express internals for contributing to Express
learn how res.send and res.json are implemented
notable: Mirrors Express's own code, variable names, and structure so readers can map it to the real library
Chapter-by-chapter build-up covering next(), routing, and response extensions
Explicitly aimed at explaining why next and route order behave as they do
caveats: Work in progress; the error handling chapter is marked WIP
Not a production web framework; it is an educational reimplementation
